summary: NASA and its partners are accelerating lunar lander development for planned 2028 moon missions while outlining flight plans for the Artemis III mission to test future landing operations. In military space developments, the U.S. Space Force awarded six operational contracts to establish a commercial reserve fleet for space monitoring, while preparing to issue requests for information on cislunar warfare concepts. Orbiting security remains in focus as Russia tails a Ukraine-linked U.S. satellite, prompting Kyiv to pursue a planned sovereign communications network with Nokia and ICEYE, while the Department of Defense selected Orbital Operations for a cryogenic spacecraft demonstration. In launch operations, Rocket Lab successfully orbited three Hawk signals intelligence satellites and SpaceX launched Starlink satellites from California, while Europe’s reusable Space Rider prototype crashed during a drop test. In space science, NASA formally concluded its long-running Swift mission, the James Webb Space Telescope imaged young stars forming in a nearby stellar nursery, and Hubble mapped gravitational lenses to guide targets for the future Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope. Meanwhile, deep-space operations continue as NASA’s Psyche spacecraft travels toward the asteroid belt following recent RS-25 engine testing at NASA Stennis. Looking ahead, industry leaders are preparing for an upcoming November 5 briefing on satellite mission management at the edge.
